newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: TROUBLED ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK SOFTER.
newsitem.headline: TROUBLED ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK SOFTER.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar ended a turbulent week on Friday further down on the key U.S. dollar with most players on the interbank market quoting wide bid/offer spreads to protect their positions ahead of the weekend.
"Our market has been in turmoil for the past three days and there's still a big shortage in the market," one dealer said.
Another added that the market would be pressurised further next Tuesday due to a large import payment expected to take another chunk of foreign currency off the system.
The dealers said the central Reserve Bank seemed happy to remain on the sidelines and watch the local currency fall.

In an interview with the private-owned Financial Gazette newspaper published on Friday, Reserve Bank governor Leonard Tsumba said the unit was five percent overvalued and hinted the bank would allow it to depreciate further in order to maintain export competivemess.
"But we don't know what level they (central bank) would like the dollar to reach before they come in," one dealer said.

Most of the dealers were however agreed that a national government budget unveiled on Thursday had not impacted the locl unit, saying it contained nothing to affect the foreign exchange market in the immediate term.
At Friday's close, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.4900/6000 against the U.S. dollar, deviating further from the normal one-point spread. This compared with late Thursday's 11.5000/6000.
It also lost against sterling to 19.1990/20.3500 from 19.1305/1505, to 6.3125/3165 on the mark from 6.2230/2300 and to 2.5360/5395 from 2.5050/5105 versus South Africa's rand.
